item.text: {"errors":[{"what":"“Estradiol and inhibin feed back (negative)” appears beside the pathway without a line or arrow returning to either the hypothalamus or anterior pituitary.","why_wrong":"The figure does not show the feedback loop named in its caption or identify its targets.","severity":"error"},{"what":"The connections between “Hypothalamus,” “Anterior pituitary,” and “Ovary” have no arrowheads.","why_wrong":"They do not show the direction of GnRH, LH, or FSH signaling.","severity":"misleading"},{"what":"“Estradiol and inhibin feed back (negative)” groups the two hormones into one undirected statement.","why_wrong":"Inhibin chiefly suppresses pituitary FSH, while estradiol acts at the hypothalamus and pituitary and can produce positive feedback before ovulation.","severity":"misleading"}],"legibility":5,"teaches_caption":false,"overall":5,"verdict":"The labels are readable and the organ sequence is correct, but the figure omits the feedback pathway that the caption promises to explain."}
